newsitem.title: ITALY: Decree opens way for Banco Napoli sale.
newsitem.headline: Decree opens way for Banco Napoli sale.

text.p: The Italian government has called a confidence motion for later on Wednesday on a decree covering the recapitalisation and privatisation of Banco di Napoli.

Southern Italy's main bank unveiled losses of 3.12 trillion lire ($2.0 billion) for 1995, the largest in Italian banking history, following the discovery of huge bad loans at the group which had previously been hidden from investors.

The group, which was controlled by a non-profit making foundation and run more as a political fiefdom than a viable financial business, plunged a further 674 billion lire into the red in the first half of this year.
New management was installed by the Treasury in early 1995 when the size of the problem became evident.
A restructuring programme was rapidly launched, with non-core operations put up for sale and the bank's presence in the north of the country cut back.
Below is a rough outline of what the decree aims to do with the loss-making southern Italian bank.
-- The government seeks parliamentary approval to inject two trillion lire of fresh funds into the bank via a capital increase, which will give the treasury almost 100 percent control of the group.

-- It proposes setting up a rump company to take over an unspecified amount of Banco di Napoli's bad loans. Treasury sources say some 12 trillion lire of bad loans are expected to be placed in the company. A final decision is due next month.
-- The decree also covers privatisation plans for the bank, with the Treasury asking for bids from domestic and foreign investors for 60 percent of Banco di Napoli by December 20.
-- The Treasury's remaining stake would be sold at some unspecified time in the near future.
